int_name: E ERIE AVE & N FRONT ST

result.summary: The intersection is heavily car-oriented, lacking marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals despite being controlled by traffic lights. The wide roadway and absence of refuge islands create a high-exposure environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks are visible at this signalized intersection, leaving pedestrians without a designated or protected path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: There are no visible pedestrian signal heads to indicate safe crossing intervals at the signalized intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic light mast arms and poles

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and commercial signage on the left may block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the roadway edge

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian space and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

result.summary: This signalized intersection lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and curb ramps. The presence of embedded rail tracks and a wide roadway increases exposure and creates potential tripping hazards for people crossing.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalks
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to guide pedestrians or alert drivers to crossing locations at this signalized intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway at the intersection

hazards.name: Embedded rail tracks
hazards.description: The tracks and surrounding brickwork create an uneven surface that can cause trips or catch bicycle tires.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway

hazards.name: Absence of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: Pedestrians lack dedicated signal heads, forcing them to rely on vehicular lights which may not provide sufficient crossing time.
hazards.location_in_image: On the traffic signal mast arms

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define the pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve crossing safety and predictability.

interventions.title: ADA-Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces to provide an accessible path of travel.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, unmarked intersection with a lack of designated crossing infrastructure. While sidewalks exist adjacent to buildings, there are no visible crosswalks, pedestrian signals, or curb ramps at the immediate junction, creating a high-exposure environment for people walking.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a wide, multi-lane arterial road with trolley tracks embedded in a brick-paved center median. There is a notable absence of visible pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or dedicated signals, creating a high-exposure environment for anyone attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a significant duration without a formal refuge.

hazards.name: Trolley Tracks
